spec.assertion: Proves no recovery events exist before Emma's first burst cast, and that stripping skill1 changes neither totals nor recovery-event count. Trigger is DEFENSIVE ('when attacked'); the scope-lock boss deals no damage and the sim models no incoming damage, so the 5% roll can never be reached — there is no whenAttacked TriggerDef in the schema, consistent with unreachability. FAILS under the nearest-wrong: re-keying the heal to `passive` (or `shotFired`) so it emits recoveries anyway — the passiveS1 counterfactual is asserted to produce strictly MORE recovery events than baseline, which would collapse to equality if the baseline were already spraying them. Over-crediting matters because recovery events drive teammates' on-recovery damage buffs (Crown-style).

Magnitude unobservable — the `heal` effect emits a recovery EVENT and models no HP quantity, and v1 has no HP pool. Recorded in the override note for completeness rather than asserted. Covered by the inertness assertions above.

it.skip with reason: the gate is trivially always-true at scope lock (nobody takes damage, so everyone is permanently above 90% HP) and has NO inactive case, so any assertion on it would be vacuous. Documented rather than asserted — writing a passing 'gate is active' test here would test nothing.

Proves offensive inertness two ways: (1) emptying skill2's blocks leaves totals(res) byte-identical for EVERY unit; (2) Emma emits zero buffApply carrying any offensive StatKey. SCOPE is the trap — 'Incoming healing' amplifies healing RECEIVED, not damage; there is no incoming-heal StatKey, no HP pool, and the heal effect carries no magnitude to scale. FAILS under the nearest-wrong: encoding it as a generic attackDamagePct/atkPct 13.33 team buff (the classic scope mis-encode from taxonomy item 1), which would move every unit's total and light up the offensive-stat filter.

Proves the recovery events reach more than one distinct target. No 'except self' clause, so target is allies INCLUDING self. FAILS under a self-only mis-scope ({kind:'self'}), which yields exactly one distinct target slug/idx.

Trigger identity: the block lives in Emma's OWN burst slot with no 'entering Full Burst' clause, so it is burstCast, not fullBurstEnter. Proves every recovery frame is at or after a burstCast frame and none precede the first cast. FAILS under the fullBurstEnter mis-key, which would place recoveries at FB-start frames independent of Emma's own cast (the divergence the taxonomy flags for multi-same-tier comps). The 39.6%-of-Max-HP magnitude is a GAP (it.skip) — the heal effect models no HP amount.

DURATION SEMANTICS: 'over 5 sec' is wall-clock and, under the heal-effect contract, a HoT sets ticks:N (intervalSec default 1) so it emits N recovery events across the window — each tick is what keeps an on-recovery consumer refreshed. Proves >1 recovery event within a single burst window, with a non-zero frame span bounded by 300 frames (5s @ 60fps). FAILS under the nearest-wrong: the whole burst collapsed into one instant heal (exactly one recovery per cast → span 0), which gives a downstream consumer one refresh instead of five. Also fails a same-frame event burst. The 39.6%-of-attack-damage magnitude is a GAP.

Whole-kit invariant: Emma emits zero damage events in the burst slot, zero offensive-stat buffApply, zero boss damageTakenPct debuff (casterIdx===null && targetIdx===null filter), and zero weapon-state buffs (reload/ammo/fire-rate/attack-speed/charge-speed). FAILS if a future edit invents a flatDamage rider or an ATK buff to 'explain' a board gap — the measured>fudge guard, encoded as a test.

fixtures: controlComp('emma', true) — the standard control comp with the fixed B3 slot enabled. Emma is Burst I so she fills the B1 role herself; the fixture's B2 + B3 units are required for the chain to complete so her burst actually casts and Full Bursts actually occur (a rotation that never completes would make every burst assertion vacuous — hence the explicit non-vacuity block asserting >=2 Emma burstCasts and >=2 fullBurstStarts). Deterministic, no seed. Four hoisted 180s runs total: baseline; skill2-emptied (offensive-inertness counterfactual); skill1-emptied (scope-lock-inertness counterfactual); skill1 re-keyed to a passive heal (the nearest-wrong discriminator proving the baseline is not already spraying recoveries). The fixed-B3 flag is left true because Emma grants no offensive stat, so the helm slot's buffs cannot confound any assertion here — every damage comparison is an equality against a sibling run with the identical B3.
gaps: it.skip — skill2 'Incoming healing ▲ 13.33%': no primitive exists. There is no incoming-heal StatKey in the schema, no HP pool in v1, and the `heal` effect carries no HP magnitude, so there is nothing for the amplifier to scale. Unobservable payload; belongs verbatim in unmodeled.skill2.

it.skip — skill2 'Activates when above 90% HP': the gate is unobservable. The sim models no HP loss (immortal team, boss deals no damage), so the condition is trivially always-true with no inactive case to discriminate against; asserting it would be vacuous.

it.skip — burst healed AMOUNTS (39.6% of the skill user's final Max HP; 39.6% of attack damage): the heal effect models no HP quantity, so neither magnitude is assertable. Record both in the override note for kit completeness.

NOT an it.skip but flagged: skill1's 'when attacked' trigger has no TriggerDef in the schema at all. It is unreachable at scope lock rather than merely unmodeled, so the correct authoring is unmodeled.skill1 text plus the inertness pins above — NOT an invented passive/interval trigger, which would over-credit any on-recovery consumer.
